Assessment incorporating SLOOS and Beige Book: The FOMC’s decision to begin a measured taper while keeping rates at 0–1/4% is consistent with a constructive outlook. SLOOS adds a slight positive tilt via broadly easier bank lending standards (housing, CRE, consumer credit) and expectations for stronger C&I and credit card demand ahead, supporting near-term growth and credit flow. The latest Beige Book corroborates ongoing expansion but flags meaningful headwinds: Delta-variant drag, acute supply-chain disruptions, and widespread labor shortages constraining activity, including autos; districts reported elevated price pressures fueled by goods and raw materials and broadening wage growth. Consumer spending remained a relative bright spot. Together, these point to supportive credit conditions amid persistent capacity and price pressures, keeping the tone constructive but cautious as taper proceeds and vigilance on financial stability risks remains warranted.

Key sentence: “In light of the substantial further progress the economy has made toward the Committee’s goals since last December, the Committee decided to begin reducing the monthly pace of its net asset purchases.”
